conditions.label: Other pulmonary embolism without acute cor pulmonale

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up three months after the October PE. Feels well, back to her normal pace, exercise tolerance good. No chest pain, no palpitations, no leg swelling. The West Coast trip in November went fine. No bleeding on apixaban; finishing the last of the bottle this week.
Mood a bit flat with the dark months, PHQ-9 7, no self-harm thoughts; still declines treatment.
Headaches unchanged.
Smoking about a pack a day. Talked about it again, she is thinking about it.

Vitals as recorded. Lungs clear, heart regular, calves soft and symmetric.

A/P:
1. Recurrent PE, both after long-haul flights: 3-month course complete, stopping apixaban as planned. Strict travel precautions on every flight over 4 hours. Call or go to the ED for any recurrence of breathlessness.
2. Mild depression: monitoring.
3. Tobacco: counseled.
RTC 6 months.

results.test: Carbon dioxide partial pressure in Arterial blood

reports.text: Sinus tachycardia, rate 116. Normal axis. Intervals normal. No acute ST changes.
Portable AP view. Lungs clear. No effusion, consolidation or pneumothorax. Cardiac silhouette normal.

CT pulmonary angiogram with IV contrast. Diagnostic opacification. Wedge-shaped perfusion defect in the right lower lobe consistent with acute pulmonary embolism. No left-sided filling defect; the prior left lower lobe clot is not seen. Main pulmonary artery caliber normal. No pleural effusion.
reports.conclusion: Acute pulmonary embolism, right lower lobe.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital, internal medicine service. Admitted 04/08/2026, discharged 04/11/2026.

Principal diagnosis: acute pulmonary embolism, right lower lobe (third lifetime episode).

Presentation: 41-year-old woman with pulmonary emboli in April and October 2025 who came in after abrupt breathlessness and chest tightness, worse with a deep breath, that began while she was out shopping. She said it felt like the earlier clots but harder to breathe. No fever or sputum, no known lung disease, never diagnosed with asthma or COPD. No leg swelling; some soreness in the right calf the day before that went away on its own. Flew Los Angeles to Tokyo one week before. Only home medication: combined oral contraceptive (ethinyl estradiol/norgestimate). No drug allergies. Smoker, about 20 pack-years. Desk-based travel agent.
Family history: mother DVT at 45, father hypertension, paternal uncle PE.

Admission exam: T 36.8 C, BP 108/72, P 116, RR 30, SpO2 91% on room air. Anxious, tachypneic, using accessory muscles. Regular rhythm, loud P2. Lungs clear.

Studies: ABG pH 7.49, PaCO2 29. CBC and BMP within normal limits; urine hCG negative. CXR unremarkable. ECG sinus tachycardia. CTPA: wedge-shaped perfusion defect in the right lower lobe.

Hospital course: started on apixaban 10 mg twice daily the evening of admission. Nasal cannula oxygen for the first day and a half, then off with comfortable breathing at rest and with walking the halls. Heart rate settled over 48 hours. Repeat CBC stable. No bleeding.
With three venous thromboembolic events, the last two while on an estrogen-containing pill, anticoagulation is now planned indefinitely. The combined pill was stopped and she was told to avoid all estrogen-containing contraception; she will discuss alternatives for her cycles with her PCP and gynecology.

Discharge medications: apixaban 10 mg BID through 4/14, then 5 mg BID, no planned stop date. STOP ethinyl estradiol/norgestimate.
Follow-up: PCP within one week.
Condition at discharge: stable, ambulatory, room air.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Discharge summary came in this morning (admitted 4/8 to 4/11 for a third PE). Called pt. Home, resting, breathing easier day by day, gets winded with laundry stairs. Taking apixaban 2 tabs twice daily until tomorrow then 1 twice daily, has the bottle in hand. Stopped her pill as the hospital told her. No bleeding. Appt with PCP Thursday 4/16 confirmed.

orders.reason: Irregular menses; non-estrogen contraception after recurrent PE

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Five days after discharge from a 3-night admission for her third pulmonary embolism, right lower lobe on CT, one week after a flight to Tokyo. Discharge summary reviewed.

Breathing improving each day; short of breath on one flight of stairs, none at rest. No chest pain, no hemoptysis, no leg swelling or pain. Now on apixaban 5 mg BID after the 10 mg week. No bleeding, no dark stools. Stopped the combined pill on 4/11. Worried about what her periods will do off it and what to use for contraception now.
Shaken by this one. PHQ-9 8. Sleeping poorly the first few nights, better now. No self-harm thoughts. Declines medication or counseling but agreed to message if it gets worse.
Smoking: still about a pack a day.

Vitals as recorded, saturation normal at rest. Looks well, speaking full sentences. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Calves soft, no asymmetry.

A/P:
1. Third PE, recurrent VTE: apixaban 5 mg BID indefinitely per the hospital team and I agree. Updated the problem and medication lists. Reviewed bleeding precautions, acetaminophen rather than NSAIDs for headaches, and taking every dose on schedule during travel.
2. Combined estrogen pill stopped; no estrogen products going forward. Referral to gynecology for irregular menses and a non-estrogen contraceptive plan.
3. Tobacco: told her plainly that quitting is one of the few things that lowers her clot risk that she controls; she will think about it.
4. Mild depression: rescreen at next visit.
Follow up in about 10 weeks with CBC and BMP.

documents.title: Prior authorization: apixaban
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy says her plan wants a prior authorization for apixaban beyond the discharge supply. Submitted through the insurer portal with diagnosis of recurrent PE, indefinite therapy. Approved same day for 12 months. Pharmacy notified, 90-day supply going through.

documents.title: Gynecology appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, the gyn office called me back but their first opening is in late summer and I'm traveling a lot in June. Is it ok if I wait to schedule? My period came late this month, which I guess is my normal without the pill.

documents.title: RE: Gynecology appointment
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's fine, the referral stays open. Irregular cycles are what we'd expect off the pill. Until you've seen them, please use condoms for contraception, and don't start any hormonal method without checking with us first. Keep your July appointment with me.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up on long-term apixaban, about 12 weeks after the April admission.

Back to full activity. No breathlessness, chest pain or leg symptoms. Flew to two conferences in June, walked the aisle, no trouble. Takes apixaban twice a day with phone reminders, maybe one late dose. No bleeding, bruising or dark stools.
Cycles irregular off the pill, as before she started it. Using condoms. Has not booked with gynecology yet; plans to call once her travel calms down.
Mood better than in April, PHQ-9 6.
Headaches a couple a month, acetaminophen helps.
Smoking about a pack a day.

Vitals as recorded. Well-appearing. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema, calves symmetric.

A/P:
1. Recurrent PE on indefinite apixaban 5 mg BID: doing well. CBC and BMP today. Refills through the PA period.
2. Irregular menses / contraception: gynecology referral still open; encouraged her to book.
3. Mild depression: stable.
4. Tobacco: counseled again.
Physical in the fall; Pap due this year and mammogram is overdue, both to be arranged then.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Morgan, yesterday's blood count and kidney tests are normal. No sign of blood loss and your kidneys are clearing the apixaban fine. Same dose.
